items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the correction law, in relation to providing identification
cards to incarcerated individuals upon release from incarceration
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8083

SPONSOR: CLEARE
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the correction law, in relation to providing identifica-
tion cards to incarcerated individuals upon release from incarceration

 
PURPOSE:

To improve the re-entry of formerly incarcerated individuals by removing
an unnecessary stigma and help those individuals become productive
members of society by giving them the same documentation as any other
person.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 creates a new section 11 of the Corrections Law to require the
commissioner of Corrections and Community Supervision to work together
with the commissioner of Motor Vehicles to provide state identity cards
to convicts leaving the custody of the department of Corrections and
Community Supervision or the federal bureau of prisons, if those leaving
federal prison are New York residents. This identification card shall be
identical to the non-driver identification card issued by the Department
of Motor Vehicles and shall be free of charge.

Section 2 renders ineffective any regulations that hinder the execution
of this law.

 
EXISTING LAW:

None

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Individuals leaving incarceration face a number of obstacles to
re-building their lives and becoming productive citizens. Many of life's
necessities, including opening a bank account, getting an apartment or
applying for a job can require providing photo identification issued by
a government entity. Currently, those leaving custody can get an iden-
tification card from the Department of Corrections and Community Super-
vision. However, this card clearly identifies this person as a former
convict. As such, it adds a level of stigma to those who use it. Getting
a state non-driving identity card at a DMV or County Clerk's office,
carries a fee, and can take two weeks to process. Removing these obsta-
cles will help those re-entering in t heir efforts to become productive
members of society.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None
 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
The first of the year following passage.

BILL NUMBER: S8083A

SPONSOR: CLEARE
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the correction law and the vehicle and traffic law, in
relation to providing identification cards to incarcerated individuals
upon release from incarceration

 
PURPOSE:

To improve the re-entry of formerly incarcerated individuals by removing
an unnecessary stigma and help those individuals become productive
members of society by giving them the same documentation as any other
person.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Creates a new Identification Card Program for those about to be released
from incarceration-requires participation between DOCCS & DMV; includes
authorization language, dispensation guidelines and fee waiver.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Individuals leaving incarceration face a number of obstacles to
re-building their lives and becoming productive citizens. Many of life's
necessities, including opening a bank account, getting an apartment or
applying for a job can require providing photo identification issued by
a government entity. Currently, those leaving custody can get an iden-
tification card from the Department of Corrections and Community Super-
vision. However, this card clearly identifies this person as a former
convict. As such, it adds a level of stigma to those who use it. Getting
a state non-driving identity card at a DMV or County Clerk's office,
carries a fee, and can take two weeks to process. Removing these obsta-
cles will help those re-entering in their efforts to become productive
members of society.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

Amended on 2.17.22

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

De Minimis.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
April first of the year following passage.

summary: Directs the commissioner of corrections and community supervision, in consultation with the commissioner of motor vehicles, to develop a program to provide an identification card to each incarcerated individual upon the release of such incarcerated individual from custody.
